criteria.name: Statistical evidence
criteria.question: Is the average IC distinguishable from zero after accounting for overlapping returns?
criteria.why: Below 2, the result is consistent with noise; Harvey, Liu & Zhu (2016) argue for ~3 given how many factors have been tried in the literature.

criteria.name: Multiple-testing adjusted
criteria.question: Does it survive the number of variants we tried?
criteria.threshold: Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across the parameter grid
criteria.why: Searching many lookbacks and horizons and reporting the best one inflates significance; Holm controls the chance of ANY false discovery.

criteria.name: Stability over time
criteria.question: Does the effect have the same sign in most years?
criteria.threshold: Same sign as full-sample IC in ≥ 75% of years
criteria.why: An effect driven by one episode is a story about that episode, not a repeatable signal.

criteria.name: Survives factor controls
criteria.question: Is it more than beta, size, reversal, momentum, volatility and sector?
criteria.threshold: Fama-MacBeth t ≥ 2 with all controls, same sign
criteria.why: If known factors explain the signal, it is a repackaging of cheap, already-owned exposures, not new alpha.

criteria.name: Out-of-sample (walk-forward)
criteria.question: Does re-selecting parameters using only past data still work on the next quarter?
criteria.why: In-sample selection always looks better than reality; this is the closest we get to live trading without spending the holdout.

criteria.name: Economic significance
criteria.question: After realistic costs, does the portfolio earn a worthwhile risk-adjusted return?
criteria.threshold: Net Sharpe ≥ 0.5 at the assumed AUM
criteria.why: A statistically significant IC can still be too small, or too fast-decaying, to pay for trading.

criteria.name: Cost margin of safety
criteria.question: How wrong can our cost model be before profits vanish?
criteria.why: Cost models for free data are rough; strategies that only work with optimistic costs usually fail in production.

criteria.name: Deflated Sharpe
criteria.question: Is the Sharpe higher than the best of N lucky trials?
criteria.why: Corrects the Sharpe for the number of configurations tried and for non-normal returns (Bailey & López de Prado, 2014).

criteria.name: Holdout confirmation
criteria.question: Does it work on untouched 2017-18 data?
criteria.threshold: Same sign and |t| ≥ 1.5 on the holdout
criteria.why: The holdout is opened once, after the specification is frozen.

criteria.name: Data adequacy
criteria.question: Is the dataset good enough for a production decision?
criteria.threshold: Survivorship-free, ≥ 10 years, point-in-time, with spreads & events
criteria.why: Free data caps how far ANY conclusion can go: at best 'worth testing on institutional data'.
